name: field
about: a realistic tactical shooter's in-game HUD: quiet, thin, honest — the world is the screen, the HUD only reports
world: a realistic shooter (the preview paints the kit default sky and ground: no game footage)
bans: plates, cutouts, chrome, glow halos or leaning blocks (the stylized identities): the realistic HUD reports and gets out of the way
big or saturated colour fields: colour is a SIGNAL only (amber objective, blue friend, red damage)
rounded corners, pills, gloss (the sim identity)
text without a soft dark edge: white on bright sand vanishes (the backdrop is a sunlit frame on purpose)
anything in the middle third except the crosshair dot, hit markers and world markers

references.take: bottom-right ammo block: magazine count tall condensed numerals, reserve smaller beneath-right, weapon name above a thin full-width bar, fire-mode tag in a tiny translucent box, equipment icons with key letters; top-left a translucent dark square minimap with a 1 px pale border
bottom-left a round compass, bottom-right two small gadget icons with x-counts over a split ammo box (magazine | reserve) — numbers in a quiet translucent box

references.game: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III — weapon HUD icon
references.take: a weapon icon is the gun's SIDE VIEW as a white outline with interior detail lines and a near-clear body — kit ui ink --mode icon from a real side render

rules.evidence: realistic HUDs measured: no leaning blocks, no fields; the amber signal is a few markers (well under 3 % of the frame)

typed_hero_evidence: assets/ui/refs/field/field_wiki_11.jpg: the real HUD sets its hero readout (the magazine count) in plain tall condensed numerals with no lettering or effect - a realistic HUD's medium IS the typed readout (owner rated FieldHud v2 80/100, 2026-10-14)
